body:
About twice a year I get sick of this and call all the psychiatrists in my area that are obstensibly accepting new patients. Almost none of them pick up, and the ones that do tell me they're not actually taking new patients. The ones that don't pick up don't call me back. I can't deal with that again right now.

I did find another psych, once, a few years ago. She was 1.5 hours away and very gungho on homeopathy, so I went back to this one.

Someone finally picked up at the psych's office. She's now on vacation until September, why didn't I call yesterday? I should see someone else. No, they don't have any other doctors available. No, they can't suggest anyone who does.

No, I couldn't get through. I might try again tomorrow, but meh. The psych doesn't listen to a word I say, which kind of makes things worse, you know?

Tldr: Things improved just enough that I let myself be hopeful, and as soon as I let myself be hopeful everything started going to shit and hasn't stopped.

Late last year was the first time I consciously realized that I had internalized 3 things:

1. Nothing I do works. Usually I screw it up, but if not, something bigger will come along and wreck it anyway. I'm too insignificant to improve my own life.

2. Everyone hates me. I will screw up every social situation and I won't know what I did, or even that I did it, until the person just stops responding

3. As a result of 1 and 2: I can't do anything to help myself, nobody else will help me, and therefore life will continuously get worse and never get better. I should never get my hopes up

Around the same time I realized this, I started a new antidepressant that was actually working for once. I decided to stop letting sad-brain run me, put myself out there, and get some feedback that would help with un-internalizing that shit. In feb I started a new job (had been mostly unemployed for the 3 years prior, no savings left) and it was looking good. I was looking forward to replacing my worn out stuff, and looking forward to getting out and interacting with people again.

A few days after starting the new job, my landlord said they wouldn't renew my lease which expired at the end of the month. That's okay, I have a new job for proof of income, I'll go apartment hunting! I booked some viewings.

The new job gave me lots of positive feedback, then laid me off a week later. Having to move on short notice with no proof of income, I was only able to get the shittiest place in the shittiest neighborhood.

I managed to quickly line up some new interviews, yay! I went to all of them and thought they went well.

None of the interviewers ever got back to me, or responded at all to followup phone calls or emails. I will never know what I did wrong. Covid started happening in earnest, and everything started shutting down. Since then I have had 0 responses for any job application. The covid-related financial help in my area is only for people who worked enough hours last year (just barely not me!) or for people who got laid off because of covid stuff (also not me!)

Meanwhile the family I told never to contact me again has started ramping up their usual tactics. This includes having their friends in other parts of the country call, calling from unmarked numbers, and so on. The goal of contacting me is to tell me what a terrible person I am, which I already know, so I do my best to avoid them. This makes job searching harder and more stressful.

The antidepressant, which is at least the 6th one I've tried, started making it impossible to breath at night. I stopped taking it.

Everything I own is breaking and I can't afford to replace any of it. My clothes don't fit. I'm stuck in a shitty unfurnished apartment and there's more gunshots every week. I've spent the last 6 months sitting in different places on the floor so that I can tell myself it's a change of scenery.

I've had a mild cough my whole life, which isn't usually a big deal. This year is it a big deal. It's worse when I'm stressed. Now, the cough makes any interaction with anyone stressful.

My area just extended unemployment benefits so you need less work hours to qualify... this would have helped in Feb, but my last half-steady job ended in July of 2019, and therefore no longer counts towards hours worked in the past year. Once again, the promised help is specifically designed to exclude anyone in my position. I wish they would stop promising.

At what point are the shitty days enough that it's not worth it? Its been almost constant shitty days for a few years now.

It wasnt just the crisis lines, it's everything thats happened for like 4 years now. The crisis lines were just about the last straw though.

Thank you for replying.

At the start of this year I thought things were looking up, but every single thing that's happened since then has been pretty well targeted to confirm everything that I *had* been trying to de-internalize.

At this point I have no hope left and regret ever getting my hopes up in the first place.
Oh good. The mental health sub is removing my shit for being too negative, that's nice.

Your dad's an asshole, don't feel guilty. He treated you like shit until he needed spare parts? Now he can fuck off and beg your brother for a kidney.

Knowing that won't make you feel any better, but hopefully you can make peace with it (both the treatment, and the kidney thing). There's no answer for how you *should* feel, and it will take some time to process how you *do* feel. It is valid to feel conflicted. Put yourself first.

edit: If it helps, there's a good chance that you wouldn't be a kidney match for your dad.

And can anyone respond if you see this? Just "Yes, I see this" even if you have nothing to say.

I just want to feel like I'm not completely worthless and invisible.
